surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions during ALD of Ta2O5 involve the adsorption of tantalum ethoxide (Ta(OC2H5)5) and water (H2O) on the substrate. The Ta(OC2H5)5 pulse leads to the formation of surface species such as Ta-O- and the subsequent reaction with H2O to form Ta-OH and release of byproducts. The mechanism is characterized by self-limiting surface reactions, where the growth is controlled by the saturation of surface sites.
evidence: The investigation of the inﬂuence of Ta(OC2H5)5 pulse time on the ﬁlm growth rate was of particular interest due to its originality. Moreover, this pulse time plays a main role on the surface saturation and consequently on the ﬁlm homogeneity. The deposition occurred during 200 cycles at 209 /C176C. H2O pulse time and Ar purge time remained equal to 2 s. Ta(OC2H5)5 pulse time was varied from 0.2 to 4 s. On one hand, for pulse times ranging from 0.2 to 1 s, the ﬁlm was found homogeneous in thickness (Fig. 6a). On the other hand, for longer pulse times (P 2 s), more than one monolayer might be formed due to Ta(OC2H5)5 dimerization. This phenomenon could be exacerbated by increasing the pulse time. Indeed, in this case, the ﬁlm was proﬁled (Fig. 6b). This result was in good agreement with the preliminar observations done by Kukli et al.. Among the different reasons proposed by Elers et al. to explain the non-uniformity of ALD thin ﬁlms, the tpurge/tTaðOC2 H5 Þ5 ratio might be too low for longer pulse times (ﬁve times lower in our case) by increasing tTaðOC2 H5 Þ5 from 1 to 2 s without increasing tpurge (equal to 2 s). In this case, the simultaneous presence of the two precursors happened in the gas phase closed to the substrate, leading to a CVD growth rate and the non-uniformity of the layer.
